assumptions: pytest is installed in the execution environment (README states pytest is used for tests)
Python 3.x is the runtime and available as python on PATH
Running python -m pytest from the repository root puts the root on sys.path, so tests can import calculator without a conftest.py or package install
Ordinary arithmetic semantics are expected: add returns a + b, subtract returns a - b

decisions.choice: Single flat module calculator.py at the repository root, tests in tests/test_calculator.py
decisions.reason: The repo is a minimal single-module project with only README.md; a flat layout is the smallest structure that matches it.
decisions.subject: Module placement

decisions.choice: Run tests as python -m pytest tests -q from the repository root
decisions.reason: python -m pytest adds the current directory to sys.path, so calculator imports resolve without adding conftest.py, packaging, or PYTHONPATH changes.
decisions.subject: Test invocation

decisions.choice: Plain pytest test functions using assert, covering positive, negative, and zero cases
decisions.reason: Idiomatic pytest with no fixtures or dependencies; callable directly as free functions per the required API.
decisions.subject: Test style

decisions.choice: def add(a, b) and def subtract(a, b) returning a + b and a - b, with no validation or type coercion
decisions.reason: The objective specifies these names and two-argument signatures; extra validation is unrequested scope.
decisions.subject: Function signatures

risks: pytest may not be installed in the execution environment; installing it is out of scope, so the test node would fail until it is available.

Floating-point assertions can be brittle; tests prefer integer operands to avoid precision issues.
